newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's McIntosh warns competitors after bid.
newsitem.headline: Australia's McIntosh warns competitors after bid.

text.p: Australia's McIntosh Securities Ltd said on Tuesday it would become one of the region's leading financial services groups after accepting a A$117-million ($92-million) takeover bid from U.S.-based Merrill Lynch and Co Inc.
Merrill Lynch offered A$1.40 a share for Australia's only listed broker, representing a premium of about 48 percent on McIntosh's average closing price in the last 30 days.
The combined firm, to be known as Merrill Lynch (Australia) Pty Ltd, would become a market leader in most broker services at a wholesale and retail level, the companies said.
"The combination will be powerful," chairman John McIntosh told the company's annual general meeting.
"Should the merger succeed, I will leave you with a final thought -- competitors beware."

Merrill Lynch executive vice-president for corporate strategy and research, Jerome Kenney, said the U.S. securities company was also interested in moving into asset management at a later stage, but had not yet decided how this would be achieved.
"We are very positive about the outlook for this market and we expect to grow this business. We are convinced that this will become a major market for us," Kenney said.
McIntosh unanimously recommended acceptance of the bid, saying its directors would accept the offer for their stock.
McIntosh's board, management and staff hold a total of 36 percent of the company.
However, McIntosh said he was unsure whether the Dutch-based ING Bank would accept the offer for its 20-percent interest.
"We are of the view that ING will act in a rational manner, but we are not absolutely positive what their position will be," McIntosh said, adding that ING's reaction was friendly.
"My guess is that in the end that they will accept."
ING was unavailable for comment on the bid.
At 3.00 p.m. (0400 GMT), McIntosh shares were 13 cents stronger at A$1.38.
The bid, which Merrill Lynch would fund from existing cash reserves, was subject to 90-percent acceptances and U.S. and local regulatory approvals.
Merrill said it already held 19.15 percent of McIntosh.
